config.title: useClickOutside

intro.title: useClickOutside
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useClickOutside` that detects when a user clicks outside a specific element, a common pattern for closing modals, dropdowns, or popups. You'll learn how to use the `useEffect` hook to add and clean up event listeners, and how to manage references to DOM elements with the `useRef` hook. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the native JavaScript `addEventListener` method for handling click events. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that improves user interface interactions in your applications.
intro.usecase: The useClickOutside hook is essential for creating intuitive UI components that respond to user interaction outside their boundaries. You'll find this pattern in dropdown menus that close when clicking elsewhere, modal dialogs that dismiss when clicking the backdrop, and floating tooltips that disappear when users interact with other page elements. In dashboards, it's used for collapsible filter panels that close when selections are made elsewhere, and in forms for date pickers that close after date selection. This pattern improves UX by reducing visual clutter and preventing overlapping interactive elements.

objectives: Apply the useRef hook to create a mutable reference to a DOM element in a TypeScript React component.
Implement the useEffect hook to manage side effects and attach event listeners to the document.
Use TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of props for a custom hook, including optional parameters.
Construct a custom hook function that returns a ref object for attaching to DOM elements.
Execute conditional logic to check if a click event target is outside the referenced element.
Handle click events by defining an event handler function that triggers a callback when clicks occur outside the element.
Control component lifecycle by properly cleaning up event listeners in the useEffect cleanup function.
Utilize TypeScript generics to type the ref object for flexibility with different HTML element types.
Assign the created ref to a JSX element's ref attribute to establish the click boundary.
Invoke the custom hook within a functional component to implement click-outside detection behavior.
Modify the hook to accept configuration options such as excluding certain elements from triggering the callback.
Return the ref object from the custom hook so it can be attached to the target element in the component.

steps.instruction: Add a type annotation to the callback parameter of your useClickOutside hook. The callback should accept a MouseEvent parameter and return void.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can type function parameters like this: (param: Type) => ReturnType. For this hook, the callback should be typed as (event: MouseEvent) => void.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useClickOutside function signature should include a typed callback parameter: (event: MouseEvent) => void
successCriteria: callback parameter
MouseEvent type
void return type
type annotation
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've properly typed the callback parameter with (event: MouseEvent) => void. This ensures TypeScript will check that the callback receives the correct event type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the type annotation needs to be more specific. Make sure the callback is typed to accept a MouseEvent parameter and return void.

steps.hint: Use the useRef hook you imported earlier. The generic type HTMLDivElement specifies what kind of DOM element the ref will point to, and null is the initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now has a ref variable that can be attached to a DOM element to track it.
successCriteria: The code should include a ref variable declared with useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null) inside the hook body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref using useRef. This ref will be used to track a DOM element so we can detect clicks outside of it.

steps.title: Add event listener in useEffect
steps.instruction: Inside the useEffect hook, add a click event listener to the document that calls the handleClickOutside function.
steps.hint: Use document.addEventListener('click', handleClickOutside) inside the useEffect callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook now sets up a click event listener on the document that will trigger the handleClickOutside function when clicks occur.
successCriteria: The code should include document.addEventListener('click', handleClickInside) inside the useEffect callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the click event listener to the document. This will allow the hook to detect clicks anywhere on the page.

steps.feedbackWrong: The event listener wasn't added correctly. Inside the useEffect callback, you need to call document.addEventListener('click', handleClickOutside) to set up the click listener.

steps.title: Add cleanup function in useEffect
steps.instruction: Inside the useEffect hook, return a cleanup function that removes the click event listener from the document.
steps.hint: The cleanup function should call document.removeEventListener with the same event type ('click') and handler function that was added.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook now includes a cleanup function that will remove the click event listener when the component unmounts or dependencies change.
successCriteria: The useEffect callback should return a function that calls document.removeEventListener('click', handleClickOutside).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the cleanup function that removes the event listener. This prevents memory leaks when the component unmounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the cleanup function needs to specifically remove the 'click' event listener. Make sure you're calling document.removeEventListener with the same event type and handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function is missing or incorrect. Remember that useEffect should return a function that removes the event listener using document.removeEventListener('click', handleClickOutside).
